Subject: Skyline Data onboarding — PO issuance trace & line-item corrections

Hi Elena / Skyline procurement team,

Thanks again for the great kickoff yesterday. Per our agreement, we need to get a formal PO on file so we can activate dedicated capacity and set spend banding in the portal. Attached is the completed onboarding form and the PO template I populated from our side. Two items to call out up front:

- Spend cap: we discussed $200,000 annual committed spend with monthly pacing. Please confirm the billing cadence and that procurement will list the cap as an explicit field on the PO.
- Line items / SKU mapping: the draft that Skyline provided last week used internal SKU codes that don't map to our ledger. I added a proposed mapping in the second tab of the attached Excel — see rows 4–7. If you prefer, we can merge into one consolidated line per product and put optional add-ons in a separate appendix.

Can you confirm whether procurement will issue a PO number in the PR-YYYY-XXXX format (we've been coordinating numbering with finance)? Once we have the PO number we'll create the provisioning ticket and reserve capacity.

Attachments: Skyline_Onboarding_Form.pdf (PDF), skyline_po_draft.xlsx (Excel).

If helpful, Marissa can join a quick 20-min call to walk through the mapping.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sergio —

Appreciate the clear summary and the populated template. A few quick notes:

1) Can you confirm the exact legal entity name and billing address for Redwood that should appear on the PO? Our AP system is strict about matching.
2) The spend cap you listed ($200k) is higher than our standard onboarding threshold and will need procurement lead approval. I'll flag with our finance partner.
3) For SKU mapping, the attached W-9 and our vendor setup form are included — W-9 attached.

We can issue a provisional PO number for provisioning while approvals finalize; standard practice here is to add a provisional prefix (PROV-). Would that work for Redwood?

I'll loop back by EOD tomorrow after I hear from our internal finance partner.

Best,

Sergio —

Quick read: finance can't issue a final PO at the $200k cap without a signed SOW and explicit cost-center allocation. Our standard onboarding provisional limit is $100k. We can do a provisional PO (PROV-XXXXX) for immediate provisioning up to $100k, but anything above needs manager (Laura) approval.

A couple of specific asks for us to generate the PO cleanly:
- Confirm legal entity and billing address (Elena requested this).
- Confirm cost-center (e.g., ENG-PLATFORM-122) and whether this lives on Redwood or is a passthrough to the customer's account (affects ledger coding).
- Apply the SKU mapping you provided — we'll need clean line descriptions for the ERP export (no internal Redwoods IDs in the vendor-facing description).

If you want, Laura can approve a temporary limit increase to $200k for the first 60 days pending SOW. Otherwise we should scope initial provisioning to $100k and stage an increase.

Ben
Ben Carter
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference

Ben / Sergio —

I'm ok to approve a temporary bump in the provisional spend cap to $200,000 for the initial 60-day provisioning window, contingent on the following being attached to the PO:

1) A short SOW or statement of work in DocSend (link in thread) describing what the committed spend covers.
2) PO must include an explicit monthly billing cadence and a clause allowing Redwood to revert provisioning if invoicing is delinquent (30-day cure).
3) Apply the SKU mapping Sergio supplied and replace any internal SKU tokens with the customer-facing descriptions in the PO line descriptions.

Ben — please issue a provisional PO number (use prefix PROV-) so operations can create the provisioning ticket; once the SOW is signed, convert to a final PO using PR-2026-4521 as the final identifier. Include the attached checklist in the vendor note.

Sergio — confirm with Elena that the SOW link and legal billing name match the details below and we’ll proceed.

Laura Bennett
